sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球海事商船注册旗国、借鉴特拉华州公司法的非公开发行实体

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Direct Online Retail of Portable Battery Generators and Solar Panels

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association (United States – Republic of the Marshall Islands), which provides national-treatment and investment protections but no discrete income-tax treaty or BIT for tax purposes.
Pacific Island Countries Trade Agreement (PICTA), limited to regional trade in goods.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Republic of the Marshall Islands Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Act 2012 (Public Law 2012-15), as amended by the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing (Amendment) Act 2021; Beneficial Ownership (Amendment) Act 2021 (Public Law 2021-08), amending the Business Corporations Act (Title 51, Marshall Islands Revised Code); Business Corporations Act, 51 MIRC §§ 10–12 (corporate names), § 18 (registered agent), § 20 (registered office), and associated Registrar of Corporations regulations on beneficial ownership registers.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport/government-issued identification of each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized consent to act as director/officer (Form 5)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the director's/officer's jurisdiction
Licensed RMI registered agent (corporate services provider)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or qualified professional reference for AML/CFT file
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-holding bank or licensed lawyer/accountant in the applicant's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory initial and ongoing screening of all beneficial owners (threshold 25%), directors, officers, authorized signatories, and any payee routing through US payment rails (Stripe, Affirm BNPL) against: (i) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (ii) the U.S. Treasury OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list; (iii) the UK HM Treasury consolidated list; (iv) EU consolidated sanctions list; and (v) RMI Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) advisories. Any politically exposed person (PEP) designation, whether foreign or domestic, triggers a six-point enhanced due diligence protocol: source-of-wealth documentation, source-of-funds evidence, written risk rating, senior-management approval, dedicated ongoing monitoring, and a transaction audit trail. Screening is conducted before incorporation, refreshed no less than quarterly thereafter, and repeated within 72 hours of any adverse-media or sanction-listing trigger.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RMI Companies Registry Online Name Clearance Portal (operated by the Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Majuro)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All filings are made in English. A corporate name must be expressed in Latin-alphabet characters; a foreign-language name may be reserved only if accompanied by an accurate English transliteration that is itself accepted as the official name. Acceptable corporate identifiers are 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', 'Company', or their abbreviations 'Corp.', 'Inc.', 'Ltd.', 'Co.'. The name must be distinguishable on the register and must not be deceptively similar to a name already reserved, registered, or available for a foreign company doing business in the Republic.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Where the Registrar rejects a proposed name, the applicant receives a written rejection notice stating the statutory ground. The applicant may file a written administrative appeal to the Registrar of Corporations within 14 calendar days of the rejection notice, attaching evidence of non-conflicting use, letters of consent from prior name holders, or ministerial approval for sensitive tokens. If the Registrar affirms the rejection, the applicant may appeal to the High Court of the Marshall Islands within 30 days under the applicable administrative procedure rules. A name reservation may be extended once for an additional 30-day period by filing a renewed reservation request and paying the statutory extension fee before the initial reservation expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address or post-office box is not permissible as a statutory registered office. Every Business Corporation must at all times maintain a physical registered office in Majuro at a street address that is open during normal business hours for service of process, together with a licensed RMI registered agent. For a non-resident, tax-exempt BC engaged in online retail outside the Marshall Islands, no operating premises, staff, inventory, or on-island activity is required; the registered-agent office may be the sole physical presence for legal service purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low but not negligible for a non-resident portable-power online retailer. Based on the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit risk matrix for non-resident low-risk e-commerce entities, the estimated probability of an unannounced on-site inspection of the registered office within the first twelve months is 5%. Unannounced inspections may lawfully occur at the registered agent's premises; inspections of foreign beneficial-owner premises are not performed without a mutual legal assistance request.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, Title 20, Chapter 1, Marshall Islands Revised Code (20 MIRC Ch. 1), as amended; applicable sections: § 9 (Lawful Purposes), § 21 (Incorporators), § 24 (General Powers), § 27 (Certificate of Incorporation), § 34 (Registered Agent and Registered Office), § 51 (Organizational Meeting of Directors), and Part VII (Non-Resident Corporations).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Marshall Islands Business Registry, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation (Articles of Incorporation) submitted in English through a duly licensed Marshall Islands Registered Agent.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow deposit required. The Non-Resident Business Corporation may authorize 1,000 no-par value shares and issue a single share for nominal consideration; no capital duty, paid-in surplus, or contribution commitment applies under the Business Corporations Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation does hereby subscribe to and accept the issuance of one share of Common Stock, no par value, issued to the sole incorporator in consideration of the undertakings set forth in the Certificate of Incorporation, and that such share be recorded in the shareholders' ledger. RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the registered office of the Corporation shall be maintained at the address of the appointed Registered Agent in Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands. RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the following persons are elected as officers, to serve until successors are duly appointed: President, Secretary, and Treasurer. RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the officers are authorized to open banking accounts, adopt the corporate seal, and execute instruments for the Corporation's online retail operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Reservation for the Business Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro; name reservation portal administered through licensed Marshall Islands Registered Agents.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request specifying the proposed corporate name, which must contain a corporate identifier ('Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', 'Corp.', 'Inc.', or 'Ltd.'). The Registrar verifies that the name is distinguishable from all registered entities and not misleading or suggestive of governmental affiliation. A reservation is valid for sixty calendar days.
required_dossiers: Certification of proposed corporate name and identifier
Registered agent engagement letter disclosing applicant identity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as confusingly similar, the applicant may, within 30 days, submit an amended request with alternative names; if the desired name is reserved by another entity, the applicant may request the Registrar's list of available variants or refile after the existing reservation lapses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Filing of the Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro; submissions accepted exclusively through the appointed Registered Agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The sole incorporator executes the Certificate of Incorporation in English, stating the corporate name, registered agent and registered office particulars, authorized share capital, corporate purpose, and the incorporator's mailing address. Deliver the executed original to the Registrar together with the Registered Agent's signed consent, the statutory government fee of USD 250, and the anti-money-laundering / beneficial ownership identification package.
required_dossiers: Consent of Registered Agent to act as statutory agent
Certified copy of beneficial owner's passport or government-issued identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a deficiency or query notice, the applicant shall submit a Certificate of Correction within 30 days, pay the applicable correction fee of USD 50, and resubmit; a clerically corrected filing is reprocessed within three business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Statutory Fees and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations — Fiscal and Filing Section.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon completion of the substantive compliance review, the Registrar stamps the Certificate of Incorporation, enters the corporation into the public register, and transmits the certified certificate and corporate extract to the Registered Agent. The entity is deemed formed on the date of the Registrar's endorsement, which must occur only after the government fee has been cleared.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If issuance is delayed beyond the confirmed service level due to internal registry backlog, the applicant may escalate to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade for administrative direction; no substantive review will be reopened absent a statutory deficiency.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Adoption of Bylaws, Registered Office, and First Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Corporate Secretary (internal statutory action; minutes maintained in the corporate records book).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting of the sole director, adopt the bylaws, elect the initial officers, approve the share subscription and stockholders' ledger entry, accept the Registered Agent's address as the registered office in Majuro, and approve the corporate seal and banking resolution. Record the First Board Resolution and consents in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Consent of Registered Agent designating registered office
Custody affidavit for minute book and stock ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an officer vacancy or documentation omission is identified, the Board may adopt a written consent in lieu of a meeting under BCA § 51 to cure the defect; failure to maintain a registered agent in good standing triggers the statutory 30-day cure period before the Registrar may commence administrative dissolution proceedings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certified Corporate Records and Certificate of Good Standing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations — Certification Division and the appointed Registered Agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request certified copies of the Certificate of Incorporation, the corporate register extract, and a Certificate of Good Standing evidencing the Non-Resident Business Corporation's valid status. These certified instruments support bank account onboarding and payment-provider underwriting (Stripe, Affirm BNPL) and verify no administrative revocation or outstanding annual compliance obligations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Good Standing request form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a Certificate of Good Standing cannot be issued due to outstanding fees or an annual report default, the applicant shall cure the arrears within 10 business days, obtain written reinstatement confirmation from the Registrar, and reapply; disputed findings may be appealed in writing to the Registrar for final administrative determination.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to Non-Resident Business Corporation status. Onshore reference authorities for any future physical presence: Business License Office, Ministry of Finance, Banking and Postal Services (RMI revenue-generating activity) and Ministry of Resources and Development (industrial trade and investment).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for offshore online retail conducted by a Non-Resident Business Corporation with no Marshall Islands nexus. A Business License under the Business License Act 1987 (Title 30, MIRC) would be triggered only if a physical place of business, fulfilment inventory, or local point-of-sale activity is established within the Republic of the Marshall Islands; the present entity does not maintain such operations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: RMI Environmental Protection Authority (EPA), Majuro Atoll, Republic of the Marshall Islands
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no Full EIA Report or environmental registration applies to a non-resident online retail enterprise without a physical project site. A Category II Full Environmental Impact Assessment would be mandated if the entity later constructs a warehouse, solar-panel assembly line, or battery refurbishment facility on RMI land.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Deemed not applicable at this stage. If a physical facility is hereafter established, the entity must comply with EPA permit terms: WHO-derived wastewater discharge limits (BOD, TSS, pH), prohibition of untreated battery acid and e-waste disposal, particulate and VOC emission thresholds under the EPA Air Quality Regulations, and hazardous-waste manifesting under the Solid Waste Management Rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable to a non-resident entity with no physical premises. If an onshore office or warehouse is later established, the following clearances would become mandatory: fire safety certification from the Majuro Fire and Rescue Department, structural and load inspection under the RMI Building Code, and occupational safety and health clearance from the RMI workplace safety program before employee occupancy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Revenue and Taxation Division, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands (Majuro); taxpayer account and filing portal: the official RMI Taxpayer Access Portal administered by the Revenue and Taxation Division. For customs matters, the RMI Customs Service operates under the same Ministry of Finance. For corporate registration, the Registrar of Corporations is the separate competent authority under the Business Corporations Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign or non-resident entity obtains its RMI tax identity through the following procedure: (i) complete incorporation with the Registrar of Corporations under the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act, or complete foreign registration if the entity is incorporated abroad; (ii) file the Revenue and Taxation Division's taxpayer registration application designated for non-resident business corporations, accompanied by the certificate of incorporation, registered agent acceptance, constitutional documents, director and shareholder particulars, and principal place of business statement; (iii) receive the statutory Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and, where applicable, a Non-Resident Business Corporation Exemption Certificate; (iv) separately register as a customs importer only if the entity will bring goods into RMI customs territory; (v) note that no VAT identification number is issued because the Republic of the Marshall Islands imposes no value-added tax, goods-and-services tax, or sales-and-use tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — the non-resident Business Corporation (MH_BC), when not carrying on trade or business within the Republic of the Marshall Islands and deriving no RMI-source income, is statutorily outside the RMI income tax net and exempt from RMI business license taxation at the national level. It is not a pass-through entity for RMI tax purposes and is not subject to entity-level RMI income tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of the Marshall Islands does not operate a check-the-box entity classification regime and does not recognize hybrid-mismatch classification elections for domestic tax purposes. Entity treatment is determined by the Business Corporations Act and by actual RMI-source activity. A non-resident Business Corporation cannot elect pass-through status in the RMI; the tax-exempt classification is automatic upon satisfaction of non-residence and no-RMI-source-income conditions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT / GST / Sales and Use Tax: Not applicable. The Republic of the Marshall Islands does not levy any value-added tax, goods-and-services tax, or sales-and-use tax on retail sales, e-commerce supplies, offshore services, or digital transactions. The only transaction-based indirect tax is customs import duty, which applies to physical importation of goods into RMI customs territory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No statutory turnover threshold exists for VAT/GST/sales-and-use tax because no such tax is imposed. The official currency is the United States dollar (USD). A person or entity carrying on business with physical or operational nexus in the RMI must obtain a local business license from the first USD of gross receipts, and must register with the Marshall Islands Social Security Administration if it employs staff. A non-resident tax-exempt Business Corporation with no RMI nexus has no indirect tax registration obligation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, XML/API clearance, or continuous transaction control mandate exists for RMI domestic or e-commerce transactions. Ordinary commercial invoices and accounting records are sufficient. For physical imports and exports, clearance is processed through the RMI Customs electronic declaration system; that system is a customs control mechanism, not a tax invoice clearance or e-invoicing platform.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Because the Republic of the Marshall Islands imposes no VAT/GST/sales-and-use tax, a statutory zero-rating claim is not applicable. At the customs duty level, goods physically exported from RMI to a foreign destination are outside the RMI duty base and may be exported duty-free if supported by evidence of removal from RMI customs territory. For the direct-to-online-consumer retail model described by ISIC 4791, if the portable power and solar goods are shipped from a foreign fulfillment warehouse directly to a foreign consumer, the goods never enter RMI customs territory and no RMI export declaration or zero-rating claim is required. If goods are first imported into RMI and subsequently re-exported, duty-free export treatment may be claimed with the RMI Customs Service subject to timely export and documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: RMI Customs Export Declaration (fully completed and electronically filed)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical removal from RMI customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank receipt evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Certificate of Origin, where preferential or duty-free tariff treatment is claimed
Re-export authorization or certificate of non-manipulation, where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Any fraudulent or abusive reliance on export duty-free or zero-rated treatment is subject to RMI tax and customs audit, retrospective assessment and clawback of all avoided duties or taxes, monetary penalties of up to twice the amount of duty or tax evaded, forfeiture of the relevant goods, suspension or revocation of the taxpayer's customs registration and TIN status, criminal fines, and imprisonment for false declarations or fraudulent export documentation. The burden of proving that goods were exported and proceeds repatriated remains on the taxpayer.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) has no central bank, no foreign-exchange control authority, and no monetary policy instrument of its own; the U.S. dollar is the official legal tender under the Compact of Free Association. Prudential licensing and supervision of banks, trust companies, and money transmitters are administered by the Office of the Banking Commissioner within the Ministry of Finance pursuant to the Banking Act 1987 (as amended); AML/CFT supervision and reporting are executed by the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit and the National Task Force under the Financial Transactions Reporting Act 2000. RMI is a member of the Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG) and has harmonized its framework to FATF Recommendations; however, no RMI statutory body is empowered to approve, withhold, or license cross-border payment flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Because the U.S. dollar is domestic legal tender, the RMI is de facto fully convertible. There is no separate capital-account versus current-account licensing regime, no stamp-duty tax on remittances, and no central-bank approval gate for cross-border transfers. Capital contributions, dividends, and profit remittances from an RMI Business Corporation (BC) are not subject to withholding taxes or FX surrender requirements. For this e-commerce entity, the only practical remittance hurdles are: (1) bank or EMI KYC and source-of-funds verification; (2) U.S. correspondent-bank de-risking of RMI-licensed banks; (3) FATCA, IRS Form W-8/W-9, and U.S. EIN reporting where a U.S. settlement account is used; and (4) merchant-of-record settlement rules imposed by Stripe and Affirm. A Foreign Investment Business License under the Foreign Investment Business License Act 1999 is required for a foreign investor carrying on business inside RMI territory, but pure online retail administered through a non-resident BC with no RMI office or local revenue falls outside that licensing trigger.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. RMI statute prescribes no repatriation timeline, no minimum surrender ratio, and no mandatory conversion of export proceeds, because the domestic currency is the U.S. dollar. Receipts from Stripe and Affirm settle in USD and may lawfully be held offshore indefinitely. Where trade proceeds arrive in non-USD currencies, conversion is at the commercial bank's discretion and requires no declaration to any RMI authority. In practice, the company should retain commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, and customs declarations for solar panel and portable power equipment exports; these documents are necessary to satisfy the U.S. bank's OFAC and AML narrative and to meet counterparty-country trade-verification rules (for example, PBOC and SAFE documentary checks in China for supplier payments).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.regulatory_status_and_international_scor: RMI remains subject to periodic APG/FATF-style monitoring cycles, and certain international banks and EMIs apply enhanced due diligence to RMI-incorporated non-resident entities because of historical offshore-zero-tax typologies. The jurisdiction is not treated as a wholly prohibited destination by major U.S. banks, but compliance scoring is materially higher than for domestic operating companies in OECD jurisdictions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.onboarding_notes: State-linked domestic bank; accepts resident and selected non-resident BCs; requires physical or video interview, certified corporate documents, beneficial-ownership register, and registered-agent confirmation; correspondent-bank de-risking history may constrain USD clearing via New York.

U.S.-territory bank with an RMI branch network; applies U.S.-style KYC and OFAC screens; non-resident BC acceptable where full BO disclosure, source-of-wealth statements, and a live in-person or notarized video interview are provided; stronger onward payment routing to U.S. Fedwire/CHIPS rails.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-to-High with material legal constraints. Offshore digital EMIs and neobanks (Mercury, Relay, Brex, Payoneer, Wise Business, Stripe Treasury) will generally accept an RMI BC only if the entity obtains a U.S. EIN, provides a U.S. operational address or registered-agent nexus, and passes a substance questionnaire; purely anonymous or no-nexus EMI accounts are unavailable. Affirm BNPL cannot be integrated directly by the RMI BC; it must be supplied through a U.S.-based payment facilitator or master-merchant arrangement that pays out to the U.S. settlement account. Legal constraints include FATCA entity classification, EMI policy bans on high-risk corridors and co-mingling of merchant settlement funds, and contractual restrictions on crypto-adjacent or third-party payout flows. If the RMI holding entity lacks economic substance, EMIs typically require a sub-account structure beneath the U.S. operating subsidiary rather than opening a standalone account for the RMI shell.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: RMI-licensed banks (BOMI and Bank of Guam) adopt a quasi-physical-presence posture: directors may appear by live video with an RMI-based officer, but the bank requires original or certified-notarized constitutional documents, a Certificate of Good Standing, certified passports, an executed corporate resolution authorizing account opening, and personal interview of each beneficial owner. Fully remote opening without any local nexus is not generally available. U.S. fintech rails and EMIs permit fully remote onboarding using biometric verification, Plaid-linked entity authorization, and telephonic or email confirmation of the registered agent; however, the signatory's identity must match the RMI Corporate Registry records exactly, and any name mismatch between the BC, the registered agent file, and the EMI application will trigger a compliance hold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: RMI-registered non-resident BC perceived as an offshore zero-tax shell with no underlying substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing from the RMI Registrar; board resolutions appointing officers and opening accounts; complete beneficial-ownership register; registered-agent confirmation letter; annual RMI franchise-tax and license receipts; management accounts or audited financial statements; physical operating lease; employment agreements; intercompany service agreements; centralized-management-and-control statement explaining why the operating COMI is outside RMI.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: high-volume, low-value e-commerce settlement flows consistent with card-based money-laundering or layering typologies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Stripe and Affirm processor throughput reports covering six months; merchant-of-record agreements; refund and chargeback policy; chargeback historical ratios; reconciliation between settlement payout statements and bank statements; transaction-level reporting API access granted to compliance; e-commerce terms of service; warranty and logistics contracts for portable power products.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: PEP, adverse-media, OFAC, or sanctions-list screening hit against beneficial owners or directors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passports; police clearance certificates; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statements with supporting asset/divestment documentation; notarized non-PEP declarations; company registry search report; independent background-check report from an approved provider; tax-residency certificates from the directors' jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: contradictory jurisdiction profile where incorporation is in RMI but customers, suppliers, employees, and bank activity are predominantly in the United States or China.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organizational chart evidencing the RMI BC as the holding entity and the U.S. or Chinese operating entity as the primary commercial subcontractor; intercompany agreements for IP license, supply, and merchant settlement; IRS EIN issuance letter; U.S. state business-registration filing; evidence of the U.S. operating subsidiary's bank account; inventory purchase orders and warehouse contracts; management accounts showing consolidated group activity; explanatory board resolution on the group structure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All shareholder capital injections and shareholder loans must be wire-transferred by SWIFT MT103 or Fedwire to the BC's account in the BC's exact legal name. The remitter should populate field 72 or 77B with 'Equity contribution', 'Shareholder subordinated loan' or 'Working-capital facility' as applicable and attach the share-subscription agreement or loan agreement to the bank. No RMI exchange-control authorization is required for inbound funds. Where the remitting jurisdiction enforces its own purpose codes (for example, SAFE overseas-investment codes in China or EU statistical purpose codes), the BC must provide its Certificate of Incorporation, opening-bank confirmation letter, and executed share-subscription or loan documentation. The account bank will credit only after OFAC, PEP, and sanctions screening of the BC and its beneficial owners. For merchant settlement, Stripe and Affirm settle in USD via ACH or Fedwire into the designated U.S. settlement account; the RMI BC must instruct the processors to use the exact registered legal name and U.S. EIN to prevent name-mismatch payout holds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier payments for portable battery generators and solar panels are cleared primarily by SWIFT MT103 in USD or, for purchase orders exceeding USD 250,000, by an irrevocable documentary Letter of Credit issued under UCP600 by the RMI bank through its New York correspondent and advised or confirmed by the beneficiary's bank, typically a Chinese or ASEAN bank. Every MT103 must align the commercial invoice, purchase order, HS tariff code, Incoterms, and shipment date; for China-bound remittances, the Chinese receiving bank requires a matching sales contract and the importer's customs declaration before credit, failing which the funds may be suspended under PBOC and SAFE trade-authenticity rules. Corporate card rails are not permitted for inventory settlement because of MCC restrictions and cash-advance risk; ACH push may be used only for U.S. suppliers and intra-group working-capital sweeps. Treasury should perform daily end-of-day reconciliation between the RMI accumulation account, the U.S. settlement account, and Stripe or Affirm payout statements to detect clearing failures and foreign-bank intermediary deductions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD-CNH (offshore Renminbi) deliverable forwards - permissible as OTC derivatives; booked under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Tier-1 international bank; physically or cash-settled in USD and CNH.
USD-CNY non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) - permissible for hedging onshore CNY exposure where physical delivery is unavailable; cash-settled in USD; no RMI regulatory restriction.

USD-CNH cross-currency swaps - permissible for hedging principal and interest mismatches on shareholder loans, supplier-financing facilities, or working-capital mismatches between USD settlement receipts and CNY procurement payables.
Vanilla FX options and zero-premium collars on USD-CNH - permissible as cash-flow hedges but restricted to documented underlying procurement exposure under an approved treasury risk policy.

Currency swaps referencing CNY interest-rate benchmarks - permissible where the swap is booked offshore and the RMI BC documents hedge effectiveness; hedge accounting under ASC 815 is available under U.S. GAAP used by the group.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report (Annual Confirmation Statement) under the Business Corporations Act 1990
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 1 October each calendar year; the Registrar’s filing window normally opens 1 July – 1 October.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of US$500; continued non-filing for three consecutive years triggers administrative dissolution and strike-off from the corporate register; reinstatement requires payment of all outstanding penalties, reinstatement fees, and registered agent costs.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory statutory audit is imposed on a non-resident private Business Corporation in the Marshall Islands. A compulsory audit arises only for listed entities, licensed banks or insurance companies, or when shareholders holding at least 10% of the voting shares demand an independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No local statutory GAAP is prescribed for non-resident corporations; financial statements may be prepared under IFRS or US GAAP solely for shareholder or management purposes and are not required to be filed with the Registrar.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Marshall Islands maintains no public UBO register and imposes no annual UBO filing with the Registrar. The registered agent must, under its anti-money laundering and due diligence obligations, obtain and annually confirm beneficial ownership information. Share transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members upon each transfer, and the registered agent’s internal UBO record must be updated as changes occur.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$3,000 - US$8,000 per year (only if voluntary or lender-required)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 3% on RMI-source taxable income of corporations; 0% effective for a Non-Resident Business Corporation (NRDC) holding a valid Section 182 Tax Exemption Certificate (no RMI-sourced revenue, no local business activities).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: NRDC Tax Exemption Certificate grants a 10-year renewable zero-tax holiday covering income tax, business gross revenue tax, withholding tax, franchise tax, and gross receipts tax. No minimum capital tax, no payroll tax, no net worth tax. The exemption is self-executing upon issuance of the certificate and is renewable for successive 10-year terms.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: RMI Corporate Income Tax Return (IR C-40) filed with the Revenue and Taxation Office, Ministry of Finance; paper filing accepted, no mandatory e-filing for non-resident entities except via the ‘RMI Tax Online’ portal at taxportal.mof.gov.mh for registered taxpayers.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on the 15th day of the fourth month following the close of the fiscal year (calendar-year filers: 15 April). Extension of 6 months available upon written request, but tax due must accompany the initial return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporation identification number, jurisdiction of incorporation, and registered agent details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter RMI Business Corporation certificate number and head office address; leave RMI agent block only if a licensed resident registered agent is appointed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxability category: Resident Corporation / Non-Resident Corporation / NRDC with Tax Exemption Certificate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mark ‘NRDC Exempt’ and attach a copy of the Tax Exemption Certificate; no taxable income schedules required when the exemption is in force.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue derived from sources within the Republic of the Marshall Islands.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter USD 0 unless the entity has storage, employees, or delivery infrastructure in RMI territory; online sales to RMI consumers are generally not RMI-source unless a fixed place of business exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions attributable to RMI-source gross revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete only if Box 2 is non-zero; for exempt NRDCs leave blank and reference the exemption.
Report 0 for exempt NRDC; otherwise taxable income is subject to 3% corporate rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable at 3%, credits, prior payments, and net amount remitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exempt NRDC enters 0 and signs the declaration statement confirming no RMI-source activity during the tax year.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of tax due per month or fraction, capped at 25%. Late payment: interest at 12% per annum compounded daily. Failure to file for an exempt NRDC: deemed revocation of Tax Exemption Certificate after 90 days of Registry notification, plus a USD 500 administrative penalty and loss of zero-tax status for the current year.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: RMI Business Corporation Annual Report (Form BC-AR) filed with the Registrar of Corporations via the RMI Corporate Registry Online portal (www.rmiic.org/eregister).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on the anniversary of incorporation each year; a 60-day grace period applies after which penalties accrue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, file number, jurisdiction of incorporation, principal office address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the registered agent’s RMI address; disclose the foreign operational address (non-RMI) for the e-commerce business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal names and addresses of all directors and officers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No RMI resident director requirement; natural person directors or corporate directors permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Record of shareholders or statement that a beneficial ownership register is maintained separately.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: 100% non-resident ownership is allowed; list each beneficiary on the private BO register, not on the public annual report.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Section 182 Tax Exemption Certificate indicator and expiration date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm certificate validity and renew before expiry; attach certificate endorsement if requested by the registrar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration that the corporation has not engaged in any RMI domestic business and has maintained proper books and records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State that all books and records are kept at the registered agent’s office or principal foreign address; false declarations trigger Section 160 BCA penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late annual report: USD 500 late fee plus USD 100 per month of continued default; automatic strike-off after 12 months of delinquency. Reinstatement requires accumulated fees, a reinstatement fee of USD 1,200, and a fresh certificate of compliance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Republic of the Marshall Islands maintains no comprehensive double taxation agreement network; only Tax Information Exchange Agreements (e.g., with the USA) exist, which do not provide withholding relief. No tax-residency certificate or TRC protocol is administered for dividend relief. For zero WHT evidence, a Non-Resident Business Corporation must present its valid Section 182 Tax Exemption Certificate and a copy of the annual return/declaration showing no RMI-source income to the paying bank or payment processor. The certificate acts as the statutory exemption instrument, and no administrative pre-approval is required for each dividend distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate 0% for interest, royalties, and management fees paid by a Non-Resident Business Corporation; treaty rate not applicable (no DTA). Foreign recipient jurisdictions may impose their own source taxation, so arm's-length royalty/interest pricing plus foreign tax credit planning remains critical for the US shareholder.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Not applicable in USD — the RMI has no transfer pricing legislation, no Local File/Master File obligation, and no CbC reporting threshold because exempt NRDCs are outside the corporate income tax base. De facto documentation trigger: USD 1,000,000 in related-party cross-border transactions where a foreign tax authority (e.g., IRS) or a foreign customs authority examines the RMI entity's invoicing, requiring a consistent arm's-length pricing policy to avoid a foreign permanent establishment and reallocation of profits.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Economic Substance (Implementation) Regulations 2021 apply to an RMI Business Corporation carrying on a 'relevant activity,' including a distribution and service centre. Pure e-commerce retail of portable solar generators and battery units qualifies as a distribution activity when the entity purchases goods from a manufacturing affiliate and resells them. Such entities must file an Economic Substance notification/declaration with the RMI Economic Substance Office annually. The statutory substance test is satisfied only if core income-generating activities (procurement, inventory risk, logistics decision-making) are conducted with adequate premises and staff in the RMI. A zero-substance NRDC is at high risk of failing the test; the standard practical defense is to demonstrate that all operational decisions, inventory, and personnel are located in the foreign market (e.g., a US distribution warehouse), making the RMI entity a pure holding/intermediary not engaged in a relevant activity in the RMI.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Exemption Claim
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Tax Exemption Certificate while earning RMI-source revenue, making U.S. or EU sales while failing to register for applicable foreign sales tax, or invoicing through the RMI entity to conceal a U.S. permanent establishment with agents, stock, or employees in the market territory.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Retroactive imposition of the 3% corporate tax on RMI-source revenue, interest at 12% per annum, 25% late-filing penalty, and fines up to USD 25,000 under the Revenue and Taxation Regulations. Foreign authorities may separately assert permanent establishment tax, state sales/use tax arrearages, and customs penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false exemption declarations or direct intercompany transfers without economic substance face civil restitution for diverted corporate tax, fraud penalties, and in aggravated cases personal liability for the corporation's entire foreign tax delinquency; travel bans may be imposed during revenue authority investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a zero-employee, zero-asset, nominee-directed RMI entity that merely passes funds from Stripe/Affirm to a foreign owner, with no board minutes, no separate bank account discipline, no custody of contracts, and no risk management functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure of the Economic Substance declaration: corrective order, penalty of USD 10,000 for the first year and USD 20,000 for each subsequent year, plus possible deregistration by the Registrar of Corporations. Under EU tax-good-governance scrutiny, the company may be listed as a shell entity, triggering refusal of treaty benefits from the owner's residence state.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors knowingly allowing the entity to operate as a shell are liable for civil damages to creditors and for the cost of the economic substance corrective process; repeated violations expose them to disqualification from serving as directors of any RMI company and to a 10-year travel ban.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register true beneficial owners with the RMI Registered Agent, failure to maintain the Beneficial Ownership Register, refusing disclosure to law enforcement, or structuring the ownership chain to obscure the ultimate shareholder controlling the solar e-commerce cash flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2021, fines up to USD 25,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years for the entity and the registered agent; the corporate registry may strike the company after 30 days of non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Each director remains personally liable for AML violations unless he or she can prove reasonable reliance on the registered agent; conviction triggers director disqualification, personal criminal fines up to USD 50,000, and a mandatory travel ban for the duration of incarceration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fraudulent Trading and Piercing the Corporate Veil
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the RMI BC as a judgment-proof vehicle to continue e-commerce transactions while insolvent, commingling the owner's personal funds with the company's Stripe payout account, or issuing related-party invoices with no delivery of goods to strip value from the customer-facing operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: RMI courts will pierce the BC's limited liability under the Business Corporations Act, rendering the shareholder and directors personally liable for the company's debts; civil restitution includes all misappropriated profits, treble damages in cases of intentional fraud, and a court-ordered winding-up of the corporation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal liability for fraudulent trading debts, court-ordered disqualification from corporate management, a bar from re-entry into the RMI as a director of any licensed entity, and in egregious cases extradition and imprisonment for up to 7 years under the Criminal Code for fraud and money laundering.
